text:
maria: Alert — ded-east-3 showing sustained 5xx and p99 latency spike for hosted dedicated customers. I'm opening a triage. (thread_ts: 1871234567)
ops-bot: [ALERT] ded-capacity-utilization>95% ded-east-3 pool; SLA risk. Link: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/1871
jamal: seeing the same in traces — sudden jump around 11:12 UTC. Any recent rollouts?
maria: no deploys. Noticed a KV cache eviction surge and kernel fallback counts spiking in profiler.
ryan: can you paste the quick profile?
maria: ```profile summary
kernel_choice: quant_fallback -> 58% tokens
p99_latency_ms: 410 (baseline 120)
avg_batch_wait_ms: 42
kv_cache_evictions_per_sec: 1120
hot_prefixes: ["user_stream-*/chat", "tenant-abc-gen"]
hot_node: gpu-12a (ded-east-3)
pool_state: capacity=96/100, queued_requests=230
```
sophia: that eviction/sec number looks like noisy-shard eviction. Possibly a single tenant hammering long-context gen clearing KV; that increases memory churn and pushes other models to fallback kernels.
jamal: agree — placement logs show 3 high-seq workers landed on gpu-12a due to quota allocator misread. config showed max_pods_per_node=4 but our dedicated pool policy expected 2 -> overcommit.
maria: reproducer: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood-internal/route -d '{"pool":"ded-east-3","policy":"latency-first"}'` — we used latency-first but allocator used burst policy in that zone.
ryan: immediate mitigation options?
sophia: 1) cordon gpu-12a from scheduler for latency-sensitive shards, 2) increase ded-east-3 reserved capacity by +2 nodes, 3) emergency routing: shift 10% traffic to ded-west-1; 4) pin hot tenant to dedicated isolated queue.
maria: done 1 & 3. cordoned gpu-12a; routing rule applied `rbac:route->ded-west-1:10%`. ops-bot show?
ops-bot: [ACTION] node gpu-12a cordoned by maria at 11:29 UTC. Traffic shift rule applied.
jamal: after cordon, p99 dropped to 150ms, kv evictions down to ~120/s. throughput recovered but we still see batch latency variance.
maria: collecting perf traces, attaching flame for follow-up ticket. Creating incident ticket: INT-4521, assign infra/serving.
sophia: root cause hypothesis: quota misconfig + hot KV shard from a few tenants -> eviction storms -> kernel selector sees high memory pressure, chooses fallback kernels -> increased per-token latency -> queue buildup -> SLA breach.
ryan: next steps: (a) audit quota config automation, (b) add hot-prefix detection + early isolation, (c) make kernel selector more resilient to transient evictions (probe slower fallback thresholds).
maria: will own (a) and (b), ryan will own (c). I'll update incident doc with timelines and perf exports.
sophia: thanks. adding postmortem owner and timeline. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INT-4521 created and linked to #incidents.
